description: Root writes a fixed name in /tmp, then chowns it to the console user. Tests the shared-directory trust checks and the High rating for a no-race local privilege escalation.

findings.rationale: SKILL.md Step 4, Shared-directory trust: '>' and chown (without -h) follow symlinks, and the name is fixed. Q2: a local non-admin user plants a symlink at /tmp/support-summary.txt before the run; root writes through it and then chowns the link's target to that user, who gains ownership of a root file; control: none (no -L check, no ownership check, no mktemp). Q3: the documented deployment runs this path. Q4: matches the High example 'Local privilege escalation to root that needs no race (a link or file planted before the run)'. Likelihood Expected (it gains root). No adjustment: the README leaves scope to the admin, so no fleet-wide raise. The '>' write, chown, and chmod on the same fixed path are one issue (distinct-issue test 1, same missing control).
